newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate firms, baht stronger late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate firms, baht stronger late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate rose further to 13.00-13.50 percent late on Monday against 13.00 percent earlier and 11.00-11.50 late on Friday due to political concerns and a slide on the bourse, dealers said.

"The sharp fall in the stock market triggered market concern about possible outflow of foreign funds. So people were keeping funds to buying dollars in the spot and swap markets," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
The SET index ended down 5.83 percent on across the board selling following the New Aspiration Party's (NAP) narrow win over the Democrat Party in Sunday's general election.

Before the election investors and the Thai business community had pinned their hopes on a win by the Democrats because the party was seen as having a strong economic team that could salvage Thailand's sagging economy.
The baht was stronger to 25.435-25.440 to the dollar near close against 25.445-25.450 early on strong demand for baht, dealers said.

"The dollar was heavily bidded in the morning triggered by political factors. But tighter liquidity and rising short-term baht interest rates prompted some dollar selling for baht in the afternoon," said one currency dealer.
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 10.25/11.25 satangs per dollar late against 10.50/11.50 in early morning.
The dollar/baht mid-rate was fixed at 25.42, unchanged from Friday.
